bindToken(address).details: Reverts while a caller is bound; call `unbindToken` first to migrate. WARNING: a bound RuleEngine MUST serve only `tokenContract`. The counter does not know which token minted, so every token the engine serves would consume this token's issuance budget.

params.token: The token or RuleEngine to bind. A RuleEngine MUST serve only `tokenContract`.

returns.isValid: => true if the transfer is valid, false otherwise

canTransferFrom(address,address,address,.details: Does not check balances or access rights (Access Control).

params.value: The number of tokens to transfer.

returns._0: isCompliant True if the transfer complies with policy.

params.admin: Address that receives the default admin role.
params.initialIssued_: Issuance before the rule was installed; at least the token's current supply.
params.issuanceCap_: Maximum cumulative issuance, in token base units (scaled by `10 ** decimals()`).
params.tokenContract_: Token whose mints are capped; fixed for the life of the rule.

decreaseMaxTotalSupply(uint256).details: Lowering the cap below the current supply is allowed: it freezes minting while transfers and burns continue. Emits {MaxTotalSupplyUpdated} with the previous and new cap.

params.amount: Amount to subtract, in token base units (see {maxTotalSupply}).

detectTransferRestriction(address,addres.details: See {ERC-1404} This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized

detectTransferRestrictionFrom(address,ad.details: See {ERC-1404} Add an additionnal argument `spender` This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

params.spender: The address initiating the delegated transfer.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getRoleMember(bytes32,uint256).details: Returns one of the accounts that have `role`. `index` must be a value between 0 and {getRoleMemberCount}, non-inclusive. Role bearers are not sorted in any particular way, and their ordering may change at any point. WARNING: When using {getRoleMember} and {getRoleMemberCount}, make sure you perform all queries on the same block. See the following https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/iterating-over-elements-on-enumerableset-in-openzeppelin-contracts/2296[forum post] for more information.

getRoleMemberCount(bytes32).details: Returns the number of accounts that have `role`. Can be used together with {getRoleMember} to enumerate all bearers of a role.

getRoleMembers(bytes32).details: Return all accounts that have `role` WARNING: This operation will copy the entire storage to memory, which can be quite expensive. This is designed to mostly be used by view accessors that are queried without any gas fees. Developers should keep in mind that this function has an unbounded cost, and using it as part of a state-changing function may render the function uncallable if the set grows to a point where copying to memory consumes too much gas to fit in a block.

getTokenBound().details: If multiple tokens are supported, consider using getTokenBounds().

returns._0: The address of the currently bound token.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

hasRole(bytes32,address).details: The default admin is treated as holding every role.

increaseMaxTotalSupply(uint256).details: Relative, so two independently approved increases compose (each adds its own amount), where two absolute {setMaxTotalSupply} calls computed from the same old cap would overwrite each other. Emits {MaxTotalSupplyUpdated} with the previous and new cap.

params.amount: Amount to add, in token base units (see {maxTotalSupply}).

returns._0: True if the token is bound, false otherwise.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). Emits a {RoleRevoked} event if the calling account had `role` and this call successfully revoked it. Requirements: - the caller must be `callerConfirmation`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

params.newMaxTotalSupply: New maximum total supply, in token base units (see {maxTotalSupply}).

params.newTokenContract: New token contract address; must not be the zero address.

params.interfaceId: The interface identifier, as specified in ERC-165.

returns._0: True if the interface is supported.

transferred(address,address,address,uint.details: The spender is ignored: the cap is per token, not per minter.

transferred(address,address,uint256).details: Restricted to the bound caller, since an accepted mint is recorded.

params.value: value of tokens involved in the transfer

unbindToken(address).details: Authorized by {_authorizeTokenBindingChange}. Operator warning: unbinding is an administrative operation and does not erase any state already stored downstream in a previously shared ("multi-tenant") setup.

params.token: The address of the token to unbind.

version().details: This value is useful to know which smart contract version has been used

returns.version_: A string representing the version of the token implementation (e.g., "1.0.0").

CODE_ISSUANCE_CAP_EXCEEDED().notice: Restriction code returned when cumulative issuance would exceed the cap.

CODE_MAX_TOTAL_SUPPLY_EXCEEDED().notice: Restriction code returned when the max total supply would be exceeded.

CODE_RULE_NOT_BOUND().notice: Restriction code returned while the rule has no bound caller.

CODE_SUPPLY_ORACLE_UNAVAILABLE().notice: Restriction code returned when `tokenContract.totalSupply()` reverts or the token has lost its code, so the current supply cannot be established.

COMPLIANCE_MANAGER_ROLE().notice: Role allowed to bind and unbind tokens on the compliance contract.

MAX_TOTAL_SUPPLY_ROLE().notice: Role allowed to change the cap (`setMaxTotalSupply`, `increaseMaxTotalSupply`, `decreaseMaxTotalSupply`). Repointing the observed token is not included; `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` holds this role implicitly.

bindToken(address).notice: Binds the single caller allowed to notify mints (the token, or the RuleEngine in front of it).

canReturnTransferRestrictionCode(uint8).notice: Returns whether this rule can produce the given restriction code (71, 50 or 51).

canTransferFrom(address,address,address,.notice: Checks if `spender` can transfer `value` tokens from `from` to `to` under compliance rules.

created(address,uint256).notice: Compliance hook invoked when tokens are created; no-op (a RuleEngine forwards mints as `transferred`).

decreaseMaxTotalSupply(uint256).notice: Lowers the cap by `amount`; reverts if `amount` exceeds the current cap.

destroyed(address,uint256).notice: Compliance hook invoked when tokens are destroyed; no-op (burns never restore room).

detectTransferRestriction(address,addres.notice: Returns a uint8 code to indicate if a transfer is restricted or not

detectTransferRestrictionFrom(address,ad.notice: Returns a uint8 code to indicate if a transfer is restricted or not

getTokenBound().notice: Returns the single token currently bound to this compliance contract.

isTokenBound(address).notice: Checks whether a token is currently bound.

maxTotalSupply().notice: Maximum total supply; minting that would exceed this value is rejected.

messageForTransferRestriction(uint8).notice: Returns the message for a restriction code of this rule.

remainingMintable().notice: Remaining mintable amount, or {CODE_RULE_NOT_BOUND} while no caller is bound (every mint reverts).

setTokenContract(address).notice: Updates the token contract whose total supply is checked.

supportsInterface(bytes4).notice: Indicates whether this contract supports a given interface.

totalIssued().notice: Cumulative issuance in token base units: `initialIssued` plus every recorded mint. Never decreases.

transferred(address,address,address,uint.notice: Applies the cap to an operation carrying a spender; restricted to the bound caller.

transferred(address,address,uint256).notice: Function called whenever tokens are transferred  from one wallet to another

unbindToken(address).notice: Unbinds a token contract, revoking its access to the bound-token entry points.

version().notice: Returns the current version of the token contract.
